seoDescription: Learn how to pass data between Vue components using props, including literal attributes, v-bind, kebab vs camelCase naming, binding from data, prop type validation, required and default values, and patterns to avoid mutating props directly. Covers using arrays and object-style prop declarations, default functions for objects, and using computed properties to derive or transform prop values for reactive UIs in Vue.js.

chapters.title: Introduction: What Props Are and Course Format
chapters.description: Overview of props as a way to pass information from parent to child components and the 10-minute tutorial format.

chapters.title: Simple Example: Passing a String Prop
chapters.description: Create a button component and pass a simple kebab-case string attribute from App to the Button component, and retrieve it in the child using camelCase props.

chapters.title: Binding Props with v-bind and Data
chapters.description: Use v-bind (or shorthand :) to pass expressions and data properties into props, and demonstrate reactive updates from a data change triggered by another button.

chapters.title: Interactive Example: Changing Passed Data
chapters.description: Show how updating a parent data property (via a click handler) updates the bound prop in the child, demonstrating reactivity and v-on click usage.

chapters.title: Prop Types, Required, and Default Values
chapters.description: Define props as arrays or objects, enforce types (string, number, object, array), mark props as required, and provide default values including default functions for objects.

chapters.title: Default Functions, Custom Validation, and Wrap-up
chapters.description: Show default as a function (useful for object defaults), mention custom validations, and conclude with feedback request and thanks.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Props**: properties passed from a parent component to a child component to provide data and configuration.

- **Kebab-case vs CamelCase**: use kebab-case for attribute names in templates (button-text) and camelCase for prop names inside component code (buttonText).

- **Binding props**: use **v-bind:** or the shorthand **:** to pass dynamic expressions or data properties into props; plain attributes pass literal strings.

- **Reactivity**: bound props update when the parent data changes; props are one-way: parent → child.

- **Prop declarations**: declare props as an **array** for simple names or as an **object** to define **type**, **required**, and **default**.

- **Types**: built-in validators like **String**, **Number**, **Object**, **Array** help catch incorrect prop types via console warnings.

- **Required props**: set **required: true** to enforce presence; missing required props produce console errors.

- **Default values**: use **default** for fallback values; when the prop type is an object or array, provide a **function** that returns the default.

- **Avoid mutating props**: do not change props directly in the child; derive changes with **computed properties** or local data copies.

> [!TIP] Use object-style prop declarations to document and validate expected inputs.

> [!NOTE] Console warnings help catch type mismatches but do not prevent runtime behavior.

> [!IMPORTANT] For object/array defaults, always use a factory function to return a new instance to avoid shared state across component instances.

## Simple Example: Passing a String Prop

## Prop Types, Required, and Default Values

First, instead of having an array let's switch this buttonText to define it as an object.
